reader.requirement: At COBOL-85, when a report group item's entry writes a USAGE clause, the subordinate group and elementary entries may write it again (necessarily USAGE DISPLAY at 85) and must be accepted, with the usage applying to each elementary item.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 runs ScreenReportEntryFormats (1985 formats and SR8)

reader.edition-search: BindReportEntry's same-usage check (usageText vs inheritedUsage) has no edition test (grep DialectLevel/Edition.Year in the member's USAGE block)
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for this rule: the repeat is accepted at every edition; 2002+ adds 'the same usage shall be specified', which at 85 cannot be violated because only DISPLAY exists
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f10_02 repeats DISPLAY on a subordinate LINE group and elementary entries of a DE group; not three levels in PH/CF groups or the bare DISPLAY spelling

probes.expected: USAGE DISPLAY on 01, repeated on the 03 LINE entry and on 05 elementary entries (USAGE IS DISPLAY / DISPLAY), accepted and printed
a differing non-DISPLAY usage is refused by SR3

citations.check: OK  §1985:XIII.3.21.3 SR2  (3.21.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: DescribeReportItem hands the enclosing entry's USAGE down as InheritedUsage; BindReportEntry refuses only a contradicting pair, which at 85 is unreachable since every legal usage is DISPLAY.

refuter.evidence: Same probe refute-1985-212/src/us_more.cob: USAGE repeated over three levels (01 with USAGE, 02 group with USAGE only or bare DISPLAY, 03 elementary with USAGE IS DISPLAY / DISPLAY) in RH, CH, DE and RF groups: accepted and printed (EXIT 0). At 85 only DISPLAY exists, so no contradicting subordinate usage is writable in a report entry. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.21.3 SR2  (3.21.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'.
